author: eval-engineer

contract.sync_assumed: none beyond warp convergence of the 32 lanes
contract.k_range: [1, MaxK] with MaxK = round_up(k, 32) <= N at compile time, k = 4 and k = 16 pay the k = 32 network
contract.n_range: N = 32 x IPT, IPT >= 1, measured 32 to 4096
contract.type_constraints: any trivially copyable key with a strict weak order, fp32 compared natively and bf16 through __hgt, int32 indices
contract.nan_behavior: comparisons with NaN are false, a NaN key lands at an unspecified position, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 and +0.0 compare equal
contract.tie_break_support: not supported in the reference: deterministic network but ties are not index resolved (not_guaranteed only). Index-in-key or (key, index) comparison would add it, see the W1 idea card
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent: the first k striped positions are sorted descending

correctness_notes: prefer_smaller_index is unsupported by WarpBitonicTopK (ties are not index resolved), those cells are listed as unsupported, not failed. Same oracle battery as B1.

low_level: No shared memory, no barriers: the latency kernel has 0 BAR.SYNC, the chain control (in-place perturbation, fold, syncwarp, read-back) is 48 cycles per call. Registers: 19 (fp32) and 26 (bf16) at N 32, 32 to 36 at N 128, 56 to 63 at N 512, 151 to 168 at N 2048, 255 with 296 to 1544 bytes of spill at N 4096 (IPT 128), where occupancy drops to 1 block of 8 warps per SM.

bf16 keys need 24 to 57 percent more SASS instructions than fp32 for the same network (1656 vs 1160 at N 128 k 16, 25512 vs 17992 at N 2048 k 16): 16-bit keys are shuffled through 32-bit lanes with pack and unpack, and the comparison is __hgt. bf16 is slower than fp32 in every cell: 778 vs 583 cycles at N 32, 2267 vs 2041 at N 128, 12606 vs 9970 at N 512, 76k vs 49k at N 2048, 156k vs 130k at N 4096.

Per input element the network costs 18 to 32 cycles for k <= 32 (fp32: 583/32, 2041/128, 9970/512, 49343/2048, 130474/4096), one shuffle latency per element per stage with no overlap inside a warp. The throughput side shows the same bound: 198 Gelem/s at N 32 falling to 88 at N 4096 (fp32), 126 to 60 (bf16), at 8 warps per block and 8 blocks per SM for the small cells.
algorithmic: MaxK is k rounded up to 32, so k 4 and k 16 cost exactly the k 32 network and share one number per N. Above 32 the cost grows with k: at N 2048 fp32, k 16 is 49k, k 64 is 66k, k 256 is 97k, k 1024 is 132k. Sorting MaxK items per chunk and merging MaxK is O(MaxK log^2 MaxK) per chunk and there are N/MaxK chunks, so the per element cost grows with log^2 MaxK.
Latency is linear in N for fixed MaxK (fp32 k 16: 2041, 9970, 49343 for N 128, 512, 2048 is 4.9x per 4x N) until registers run out: N 4096 costs 2.6x N 2048 because of the spills, not the network.

Against the block incumbent at matching N the warp network is an order of magnitude more expensive per element (B1 at N 4096 fp32 k 16: 3705 cycles for 4096 items, W1 at N 2048: 49k for 2048 items), so W1's place is small N (routing rows of 32 to 128) and the tail of a hierarchy, as the W1 idea card expects.

Output is sorted and deterministic for free, which no other focus-set reference gives. Ties are resolved by network position, so prefer_smaller_index needs the index inside the key or a (key, index) comparator, both of which the W1 optimizer owns.
negative: The native bf16 comparison path is a loss on this network: every cell is slower than fp32, the opposite of the hoped-for 16-bit advantage. Packing two bf16 keys per 32-bit lane (the W1 idea card's packed arrangement) is the way to turn 16 bits into a win, comparing them one by one through __hgt is not.
N 4096 at 32 lanes (128 items per lane) is past the register file: 255 registers with spills in every k, the cell is a stress point rather than a design point for a warp primitive.
surprises: The July figure for a single WarpBitonicTopK 128 to 16 call was about 2500 cycles (half of bitonic_hier's 5112 with its block barrier, smem staging and chain link), this harness measures 2041 net for the same shape and key type, consistent once the July overheads are taken out.

On GB200 the A/A control of the data-oblivious chain spreads by 2 to 4 percent at N 2048 fp32 (50216 vs 48859 at k 4, 141984 vs 136712 at k 1024) while B200 agrees to 0.01 percent, and the GB200 fp32 N 2048 k 1024 build shows 64 bytes of spill where B200 shows none at the same register count.
open_questions: Which part of the bf16 penalty is the shuffle packing and which the __hgt compare? A packed two-keys-per-lane variant answers both at once.

Does the buffered threshold-compaction variant of PR #9281 beat the eager network for N much larger than MaxK (N 512 and up at k 16), where the eager form spends 90 percent of its time sorting chunks that are then discarded?

Is the GB200 A/A spread a clock effect on a shuffle-bound chain (cycles should be clock invariant) or an SM placement effect? Worth a repeat with more repetitions before any 3 percent GB200 claim is made for a warp primitive.
